question: With 1 mmHg equal to 13.6 mm of water, how much higher is arterial pressure at ankles 1.2 m below the heart, in mmHg?
answer: About 88 mmHg higher than at the heart.
move: In any column of fluid, ask how high it stands before comparing pressures.
trap: Assuming the heart sets one pressure for the whole body.
hint: Turn the height of the column into millimetres of water first.
steps: Treat blood as water: 1.2 m is a column of 1,200 mm.
Each mmHg is 13.6 mm of water: 1,200 / 13.6 = 88.2.
About 88 mmHg higher than at the heart.
simply: At the heart, mean arterial pressure is about 90 to 100 mmHg; at the ankles of someone standing it is nearly double. The veins there gain the same extra pressure, so the push driving blood through the ankles barely changes.
reference: Rowell, Human Cardiovascular Control, Oxford University Press, 1993
